messages:
rachel: quick spike idea: implement a compact hot-range prefetch that prioritizes small, frequently-accessed tensor ranges inside safetensors shards. goal: reduce p95 cold-start for retrieval-heavy prompts without full-shard reads.

sam: short + clear, love it. whats the change surface? loader API, indexer, catalog? :eyes:

rachel: indexer: emit compact hot_ranges as byte offsets (and optionally map to tensor names). weight-catalog: accept hot_ranges as an experimental field. loader: accept hot_ranges hint and a runtime flag 'compact_prefetch=true'. scheduler: coordinate coalescing and io budget.

cheng: how do clients express hot_ranges? per-layer ranges, or global?

rachel: per-shard hot_ranges in the manifest. indexer creates them by sampling token access traces or heuristics. example inline manifest fragment in the RFC draft: 

```json
{
  "model": "qa-lt1",
  "shards": [
    {"id": "0", "size": 9876543, "hot_ranges": [[4096, 32768], [128000, 130500]]}
  ]
}
```

anita: exposing byte offsets is format-coupled. any plan to keep it format-agnostic?

luke: pragmatic approach: catalog stores hot_ranges in canonical form (byte offsets relative to the transport). indexers for other formats translate into the same canonical offsets. loader uses offsets for streaming reads; if a format cannot map to offsets we fallback to logical tensor hints.

sam: operational concerns: many small reads can blow up IOPS. how do we prevent that?

rachel: three mitigations: 1) coalesce adjacent ranges within a coalesce_window (default 64KB) into a single read, 2) async scatter-gather only on transports that support parallel range reads, 3) io_budget per-request to cap ops.

cheng: eviction weirdness: filling sparse ranges might evict a contiguous block needed by a different request. eviction strategy?
achel: introduce 'sparse-favor' eviction in the warmup scheduler: evict contiguous dense segments first if they don't intersect hot_ranges. if memory pressure is severe use LRU. also track eviction-churn metric.

anita: what telemetry do we add to validate benefit vs cost?

luke: add these metrics: hot_range_utilization, coalesce_rate, prefetch_io_ops, warmup_memory_churn, cold_start_p95_by_model. These will feed an experiment dashboard.

perf-bot: queued perf job: compact-hotrange-spike-2026-03-23-02. collecting IO traces and warmup timelines.

sam: rollout plan? start behind a feature flag? canary on dedicated pools or specific routes?

rachel: feature-flagged, default off. canary on dedicated pools and a subset of models known for skewed token access (RAG/QA). monitor p95 cold latency and io_ops delta. auto-disable for a model if prefetch_io_ops spikes or coalesce_rate low.

cheng: compatibility note: safetensors indexer can derive offsets cheaply, but some legacy checkpoints won't. need a graceful fallback path.

rachel: agreed. indexer will add hot_ranges when available. loader accepts missing hot_ranges and falls back to standard shard-eager warmup. catalog validation will warn but not block.

sam: detection heuristics to flip off the feature for a model?

luke: heuristics: if coalesce_rate < 0.5 OR prefetch_io_ops > ops_threshold for N consecutive cold loads, mark model as "prefetch-inefficient" and switch to shard-eager for that model-version. Emit an alert to #perf.

anita: edge failure cases: partial read errors, or transports that do not support range reads?

rachel: transports that lack range-read will fall back to whole-shard read. partial read errors trigger retry with backoff; repeated failures mark hot_ranges stale and fall back. indexer should incrementally verify hot_ranges in background.

perf-bot: perf run complete: compact-hotrange-spike-2026-03-23-02 results: p95 cold reduced by ~15% on canary models; prefetch_io_ops increased by ~9%. traces uploaded to S3.

sam: nice. next steps? RFC? small RFC follow-up with schema and loader API signatures?

rachel: yes - i'll prepare a short RFC that includes manifest schema, loader API patch, and the rollout checklist. will ping for review.

cheng: thanks, also please add a config knob warmup.policies.compact_mode = ["balanced","aggressive","conservative"].

rachel: noted, adding to RFC. thanks all :thumbsup:

perf-bot: experiment dashboard link: https://perf.redwood.example.org/experiments/compact-hotrange-spike-2026-03-23-02
